finding_dispositions.note: All nine cited records are bound in research/source-bindings.toml (87 bindings, role context, each stating that the page-2 Date column rests on it). The eight Catholic Encyclopedia records the corpus cites are remote New Advent deliveries whose bytes were not re-obtained, so they are bound as catalogued only; their eight tracked article-text extractions were hashed, matched to their records by SHA-256 and byte size, read at the sentence carrying each label with its paragraph, and bound as inspected with the library's fingerprints. A recomputed proper-study-v3 seal grew from 2,052 to 2,095 files: 38 under src/sources/works/catholic-encyclopedia, 4 under the NABRE edition, and the Catholic Encyclopedia rights record, newly declared in review-dependencies.toml. Twelve of the fourteen Catholic Encyclopedia labels stand verbatim as continuous wording, and the other two stand in every part: the Isaias label is a composite of lines 9 and 11 of the article, as the corpus's own basis and note say, and the Howlett label reverses the two phrases of one sentence across its ellipsis. 'about A.D. 38-45' cites Durand as well as Jacquier, and Durand's article does not contain that figure (the corpus note says he is cited for a caution, which was read). The NABRE passage is bound as catalogued only: the registered 2026-07-28 bytes are restricted and were not obtained. The page's current public delivery was fetched over verified TLS (74,081 bytes, hash recorded in scope section 5; it differs from the registered 74,094 bytes), read at the dating sentence, and not retained. Its content supports the label, which is the corpus's own summary of protected prose and not the source's wording; the source prints 'ca. 165' with no era. Both proper-chronology --check runs still report the files current.

notes: RECORDS REVISED: research/source-bindings.toml (17 bindings added: 8 cited Catholic Encyclopedia artifacts as catalogued, their 8 article-text artifacts as inspected, the NABRE Psalms introduction passage as catalogued); research/review-dependencies.toml (Catholic Encyclopedia rights record declared; comment on the nine bound sources); research/scope.md (header; section 3 normalization statement; new paragraph in 3.1 on the Migne editor's notes; section 4 Consequence; section 5 row for the NABRE delivery; new sections 8.1 and 8.2; section 9 rights; section 10 items 2 and 8); research/interpretations.md (header; Standing limits; Reading 1 Jerome row; five Element-contribution rows). No source-library record was added or changed. ADVISORIES: RES-014 cleared: PL 26 col. 141 notes a, b and c were read on the retained page image and recorded as an editor's identification of Origen (and of Hilary as drawing on him), classed as a lead, with the bound that Origen and Hilary on Matthew were not opened; this reader did not see Huet named on that page and does not say so. RES-015 cleared: five quoted English fragments about the Entrance antiphon, the Prayer over the Offerings and the Prayer after Communion are now description, with Latin words from the owner's record where useful, no first person, and a standing note that none of it is the prayer's English. RES-016 cleared by stating the normalization (i for j, ligatures written out, v for CSEL's consonantal u), with the CSEL spellings re-seen on pp. 367, 834 and 838. FOR THE CORPUS OWNER, not acted on: whether Isaiah 55 should carry a disputed state (Souvay's article reports the 'second Isaias' contention and the 1908 Biblical Commission decision and prints no year for chapters xl-lxvi), and whether a label that summarizes a protected source should be marked as a summary. GATES: tools/source-library validate passes; check-content-preflight bindings-valid and restricted-not-reproduced pass; proper-study check --phase research passes. LIMITATIONS: the printed Catholic Encyclopedia was not seen; the registered NABRE bytes were not read; make check-sources still fails only on the publication-inventory and web-edition state of this unfinished, uncommitted production, which predates this re-entry and was left to the integration phase; chronology-annotations-current in content-preflight awaits the authoring stage's format.tex.
summary: Second research re-entry for PC-S51-A: read and bound the nine source records behind the chronology corpus's answers, so the research seal now lists files under each, and recorded in scope section 8.1 what was read, in what form, and whether each of the fifteen labels stands. No date was supplied, no corpus answer altered, and nothing was regenerated; the three advisories were also cleared.
